blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

Conflicts flagged up front: (1) Ocean Park Place's built year conflicts — the building directory states 1979 while MLS listings for its units state 1978 — so the year is carried as 1978–1979 UNCONFIRMED in. (2) Rockford by Cressey's unit count conflicts — the developer's own feature sheet states 63 condominium residences while presale sources state 60 condominiums — carried as a conflict, not settled, in; Rockford is a presale (estimated completion 2027 on the presale records read), NOT completed resale stock, and is documented but not counted.
Ocean Park Place — 12890 17 Avenue, Ocean Park

The building directory records the name Ocean Park Place at this address, built 1979, 54 units, with club house, elevator and storage; MLS listings for units at the address record sub-type Apartment/Condo, strata plan NWS1191, complex name "Ocean Park", and built 1978 — the year therefore conflicts (directory 1979 vs listings 1978) and is carried as 1978–1979 UNCONFIRMED. Directory restrictions: age restrictions; pets not allowed; rentals not allowed — that recorded line is VOID for long-term rentals under the Nov 24, 2022 rule in. The directory does not state the age in its restriction line; two unit listings describe the building in their text as a "55 PLUS BUILDING" and a "well-managed 55+ community" — listing text only, so the exact age bylaw is UNCONFIRMED until the registered bylaws are read, and no other age is asserted here.

items.t: "Crescent Beach Ocean Park" in full (MLS® "Crescent Bch Ocean Pk.") is one board sub-area joining two seaside communities — Crescent Beach, a low village at the mouth of the Nicomekl River below the Crescent Heights bluff, and Ocean Park, on the east side of Boundary Bay — and one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "S Surrey White Rock". The street-level board boundary is UNVERIFIED — no public street-level boundary was opened, and no municipal boundary was substituted.
White Rock's own bylaws (Zoning Bylaw 2024 No. 2506 / OCP Bylaw 2017 No. 2220) belong to White Rock only and are never applied to a Surrey-address building here.

Community context only (whole S Surrey White Rock community, NOT this sub-area's prices): Detached median $1,628,000; Condos & Townhomes median $700,000 / $524 per sq ft / 99% sale-to-list / 33 DOM. Per-sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level.

Beach and parks, as the guide page states them citing the City of Surrey: Crescent Beach at 12160 Beecher Street, open dawn to dusk, two roped swim areas, summer lifeguards at Sullivan Point, a pier and a beachfront path on the 1913 dykes; Blackie Spit Park at 3136 McBride Avenue; Kwomais Point Park at 1367 128 Street; Crescent Park at 2585 132 Street, a 52-hectare forested park. Transit routes 350 and 361 are stated on the guide page as site copy only — no timetable was opened, so routes, stops and frequencies are UNVERIFIED here.

Flooding, as the guide page states it: Crescent Beach sits 0 to 3 metres above sea level inside a dyke system, a 1982 storm surge heavily damaged frontage properties, and the City's Coastal Flood Adaptation Strategy (approved November 2019) covers Crescent Beach. Flood status for any specific property is UNVERIFIED.

items.t: Surrey plan and zoning: Surrey is planned under the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026) — Bylaw No. 18020 is the predecessor only, never current — with zoning under Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000, parcel by parcel. The Crescent Beach Local Area Plan guides development in Crescent Beach; the guide page adds, as its own statement, that it was approved in April 1999 and covers about 91 hectares bounded by water to the north, west and north-east.

SSMUH and suites (Surrey-wide, for detached lots here): up to 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop (City adopted the changes July 8, 2024); a secondary suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable floor area under Bylaw 12000 — a "90 m²" figure is NOT the current Surrey cap.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Crescent Beach / Ocean Park

items.t: OCP / Zoning — Surrey: Surrey Official Community Plan Bylaw 21900 (adopted Jun 15, 2026) is current — never cite 18020 as current. Surrey Zoning Bylaw 12000 governs. The Crescent Beach Local Area Plan guides Crescent Beach parcels within that frame.

SSMUH — Surrey (City position as stated): maximum 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop; the City adopted the SSMUH zoning changes on July 8, 2024.

ALR block (where ALR ground exists — parcel status here UNCONFIRMED): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

Strata block (bare-land strata parcels, if a parcel is one): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

FTHB PTT exemption: first $500,000 exempt, full at value ≤$835,000 (max saving $8,000), partial to $860,000; Newly Built Home Exemption is a new-HOME exemption (full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000).

Foreclosure / court sales (where met): a settled court process exists (BC Supreme Court Civil Rules 21-7 / 13-5, Practice Direction PD-66, Form 60); whether Form B and the PTT/GST treatment on a court-ordered sale of a lot here differ is UNCONFIRMED. Surrey has NO Supreme Court registry (registry mapping UNVERIFIED).

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Crescent Beach Park than in June?
faq.a: In Crescent Beach Park, listings of houses fell from 106 in June to 94 in September (−11.3%); condos and townhomes rose from 15 in June to 16 in September (+6.7%).

faq.q: How big is Crescent Beach Park compared with the rest of South Surrey and White Rock?
faq.a: In September 2026, Crescent Beach Park held 15.7% of the 600 houses listed in South Surrey and White Rock and 2.7% of the 593 condos and townhomes listed in South Surrey and White Rock.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Crescent Beach Park from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 48 houses and 6 condos and townhomes sold in Crescent Beach Park over those 4 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Crescent Beach Park?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Crescent Beach Park?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Are Crescent Beach and Ocean Park the same condo market?
faq.a: They are one board sub-area (Crescent Beach Ocean Park, F53), but the verified apartment stock sits entirely on the Ocean Park side: one completed building (Ocean Park Place, 12890 17 Avenue) and one presale (Rockford, 1655 128 Street). No verified apartment building stands in Crescent Beach village.

faq.q: How did the attached market do in September 2026?
faq.a: Medians are published at community level only (S Surrey White Rock attached median $700,000), not for this sub-area.

faq.q: Is Ocean Park Place a 55+ building, and can I have a pet or rent it out?
faq.a: The building directory records age restrictions and "pets not allowed", and unit listings describe a 55+ building — but the directory states no age, so the exact bylaw is UNCONFIRMED until the registered bylaws on the Form B are read; the only lawful age form is 55+ under SPA ss. 123.1/123.2. Its directory "rentals not allowed" line is void for long-term rentals since November 24, 2022.

faq.q: When was Ocean Park Place built — 1978 or 1979?
faq.a: The sources conflict: the building directory says 1979 (and 54 units, strata records under complex name "Ocean Park", plan NWS1191 in the listings), while MLS listings for its units say 1978.

faq.q: Is Rockford a resale building I can move into?
faq.a: No — on the records read it is a presale by Cressey Development Group at 128 Street and 17 Avenue, a 4-storey concrete low-rise with estimated completion 2027; even its unit count conflicts (63 residences on the developer's feature sheet, 60 condominiums on presale sources). A purchase is a developer contract: GST applies, the Newly Built Home PTT exemption is the one to check, and REDMA gives a 7-day rescission period with deposits in trust.

faq.q: Is there a condo in Crescent Beach village itself?
Is Ocean Park Place a 55+ building?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED as a bylaw. The directory records "age restrictions" without stating the age, and two unit listings call it 55+ in their text; only a 55-or-older bylaw is valid under SPA ss. 123.1/123.2 + Reg 7.01 in any case, with the exemptions in. Read the registered bylaws on the Form B package before relying on any age.

faq.q: Can I rent out an Ocean Park Place unit if the directory says rentals are not allowed?
faq.a: Long-term, yes — every BC strata rental-restriction bylaw became void on November 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw.
